solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pronouncement is difficult for this judge, criminal waiving right to counsel

parts.note: J is the standard abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: to waive something is to give it up, so a letter is surrendered from the word

parts.note: a criminal is someone who breaks the law

indicators.note: the right of a word is its end, so only the last letter is meant

parts.note: last letter, the one given up

explanation.surface: A judge notes that a defendant has waived the right to a lawyer, and says so with difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to counsel' sounds like the legal entitlement, but it is only the rightmost letter of 'counsel'. The criminal drops that L, and J goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A jawbreaker is a word so long or awkward that saying it seems to strain the mouth.

clue.text: Champion of Wimbledon playing a man and a woman

parts.note: taken as written
SHE is a woman, and it contains HE, a man, so one word plays both

explanation.surface: A tennis champion at Wimbledon plays mixed doubles against a man and a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Two routes to the same letters: 'playing a man' is AS HE, acting as him, and 'a woman' is A SHE. Either split works.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe, the American tennis player, won the men's singles title at Wimbledon in 1975.

clue.text: Woman's collection robbed of top painting

indicators.note: being robbed of the top means losing the first letter, the top of a down entry

parts.note: a bride's collection of clothes and linen gathered for her marriage

explanation.surface: A woman's art collection has been stolen from the top floor, painting and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's collection' looks like an art collection, but it is a trousseau; the painting is the answer, not part of the theft.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting by Henri Rousseau, the French naive artist, can be called a Rousseau, as a work by Monet is a Monet.

clue.text: Newgate for one bogy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old prison, since nick is British slang for jail
second meaning: a nickname for the Devil, a bogeyman

explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was a notorious London prison, long since demolished, so it is literally an old nick.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional English name for Satan, the frightening figure of folklore; Newgate was a historic jail, and nick means jail.

clue.text: Out between "4" and 19 half of 16 17 (and between 2ac and 22 anticlockwise)?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dismissed in cricket when a fielder takes the ball on the full
second meaning: the word that completes the saying built from other answers in the grid

explanation.walkthrough: 4 is OLD NICK, the devil; 19 is THE DEEP; half of 16 is BLUE and half of 17 is SEA: caught between the devil and the deep blue sea. The bracket points to the other saying, between a rock and a hard place.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman is out when caught, and someone trapped between two bad options is proverbially caught between them.

clue.text: Principles of kilt, negligée etc, sporting leg then?

definitions.text: Principles of kilt, negligée etc, sporting leg then?

indicators.note: principles sound like principals, the leading ones, so only the opening letters count

parts.note: first letter

indicators.note: sporting can mean playing about, so the letters frolic into a new order

parts.note: first letter
first letter
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion question: what rules govern kilts and nightdresses that show off a bit of leg?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: kilts and negligées are typical examples of garments cut to reach the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilt or a negligée typically hangs down to the knee, making both garments examples of that length.

clue.text: Genius provided ingredients for popular cocktail drinks

indicators.note: whatever drinks something takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: gin and tonic, a popular mix, is written G and T
provided that means if

explanation.surface: A genius at the bar makes the cocktails provided the right ingredients are there to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: G and T is the everyday British shorthand for gin and tonic, so its ingredients are the letters G and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural talent or flair, the same innate ability we call genius.

clue.text: Local supporter secures gun

parts.note: to bar a door is to secure it
slang for a firearm

explanation.surface: A fan of the local team gets hold of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local supporter' reads as a fan of a home side; in Britain the local is your neighbourhood pub, and a bar stool literally supports drinkers there.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar stool is a tall seat in a pub, holding up the regulars, so it props people up at their local.

clue.text: Abba's first release that introduced Top of the Pops!

definitions.text: that introduced Top of the Pops

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the band's name
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: Abba's first single was the record that launched the chart show Top of the Pops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' looks like a record release; it is a verb. Auntie is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC, which broadcast Top of the Pops, the weekly pop chart show.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC, nicknamed Auntie, launched and broadcast the long-running television chart programme.

clue.text: Religious, Lincoln's bishop, and special — doubly so

indicators.note: doubly means twice over, so each added letter sits beside a twin already there

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's short name, with the possessive S
B is the chess notation for bishop
S is short for special

explanation.surface: A religious man, Lincoln's bishop, is special twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln here is Abraham Lincoln, not the English cathedral city. ABE'S already has a B and an S; adding one more of each doubles both.
explanation.definitionFit: In crossword and church usage a religious is a noun meaning a monk or nun; an abbess heads a convent of nuns.

clue.text: Disregards Nigel at the outset and chooses to retain Government

indicators.note: the outset is the very start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece keeps another inside

parts.note: to elect is to choose
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A politician ignores Nigel from the start and opts to keep the government in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chooses to retain Government' reads as a vote; ELECTS is what holds the G.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to ignore it or fail to attend to it, the same as paying it no heed.

clue.text: Corrode ship's copper, paper bags do

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a sack, so one piece is packed inside another

parts.note: the Financial Times, this puzzle's own newspaper
to eat away is to corrode
a ship is referred to as she, so what belongs to it is hers
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's report on hulls: rust eats a ship's copper sheathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb at the end but is the noun for a hairstyle. The FT is the paper this crossword appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather cut is a hairstyle with the hair cut in layers; a do (hairdo) is a colloquial word for any styled haircut.

clue.text: Demagogue raised objection, wanting friend to fawn

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters lifts them bottom to top, so they run backwards

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
Thumper is the rabbit who befriends the young deer in Disney's Bambi

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser objects loudly, wanting his friend to grovel before him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' looks like a verb meaning to grovel, but it is the young deer Bambi, whose best friend is the rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub-thumper is a ranting public speaker, like one pounding a pulpit, which is what a rabble-rousing orator does.

clue.text: Some feedback from the choir

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the letters sit inside a longer run

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A listener passes on comments about the choir's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Feedback sounds like critical comments; here it is sound bouncing back, fitting a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is sound reflected back to its source, a kind of acoustic return like the howl of audio feedback.

clue.text: Surreal choice, Miro — burlesque in the extreme

indicators.note: something surreal is bizarrely distorted, so the letters are jumbled out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Picking Miró, the Spanish Surrealist painter, as your artist is outrageously over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surreal' fits Miró the painter so well it hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroi-comic describes writing that mixes heroic grandeur with comedy, the mock-epic style of burlesque pushed to its limit.

clue.text: Awfully bulky case about to split — this is a shade lighter

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters end up in a mess
to split is to leave, so those letters depart from the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
circa, about, abbreviated; these letters leave

explanation.surface: A heavy suitcase is about to burst open, which would make it a little lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like less heavy, fitting the bulky case; it is a colour paler than others. CASE loses CA and what remains is mixed with BULKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky blue is a pale tone of blue, a light shade among colours.

clue.text: Mansion maintains appearance from behind, like literary isle

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold on to, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a country seat is a grand house

indicators.note: read from behind means from the back end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rig is an outfit, how someone is turned out

explanation.surface: A stately house keeps up its looks at the back, like an island in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sea-girt is a poetic word, hence 'literary'; Shakespeare and Milton use it of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-girt means surrounded by the sea, a poetic epithet for an island encircled by water.

clue.text: Memorable, very fluent, English in translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into a different form, so the letters are recast

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A translation is praised as memorable, very fluent English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In translation' looks like praise for a translator; it is the anagram signal, and 'very' and 'English' give their abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventful period is one full of happenings, something worth remembering afterwards.

clue.text: Remote positions Scottish runner takes up, finally

parts.note: a river is a runner, and the Dee is a Scottish river

indicators.note: finally points at the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A Scottish athlete moves into far-flung positions at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; in crosswords it is often a river. The Dee flows through Aberdeenshire.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the deep is the outfield near the boundary, the fielding places furthest from the batsman.

clue.text: Main gateway?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: chief, as in an archenemy
second meaning: a curved structure one passes through

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main gateway' reads as the principal entrance; split it and each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective the word means principal or chief; as a noun it is a curved opening like a portal.

clue.text: Scientist revelling in father inhaling helium

indicators.note: to inhale is to breathe something in, so one piece goes inside another
revelling is wild partying, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A scientist enjoys himself hugely at his father's expense after breathing in helium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit was the German physicist who devised the temperature scale that bears his name.

clue.text: Was searching storage facility at Silverstone?

parts.note: F1, Formula One, with the digit read as the letter I; Silverstone is the British Grand Prix circuit
a shed is a simple store

explanation.surface: Someone hunted for a garage to keep things in at the Silverstone motor-racing circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: An F1 shed would be a racing team's store at Silverstone; reading the 1 as I turns it into a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: To fish for something is to hunt or grope about for it, as when fishing in a pocket for keys.

clue.text: In Order of Merit, is newspaper chief reduced?

parts.note: at can mean in, as in at home
OM is the abbreviation for the British honour
taken as written
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: Is a newspaper editor who has been given the Order of Merit now cut down to size?
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour limited to a few distinguished people.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomise is to break something into tiny particles or a fine spray, turning it into minute fragments.

clue.text: Plants warm up, temperature rising maximally

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising as far as possible means climbing all the way to the top

parts.note: to heat is to warm up
T, the abbreviation for temperature, is the letter that moves

explanation.surface: Warm up your plants and the temperature goes up as high as it can.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the bottom of HEAT climbs to the top of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Thea is the botanical genus name once given to the tea plant, so the plural 'plants' fits a genus.

clue.text: Saw through one's own table?

indicators.note: something that goes through another passes inside it, so one piece sits within

parts.note: on one's tod is British rhyming slang for alone, from Tod Sloan, a jockey, rhymed with own
to rip is to saw wood along the grain

explanation.surface: Would you take a saw to your own table?
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'on your Tod Sloan' means on your own, shortened to 'on your tod'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand, and the word also names a three-legged table or stool.

clue.text: Check authenticity of each plan

parts.note: to ID someone is to check who they are
ea is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Verifying that each scheme is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check authenticity' is the verb ID, to check someone's identity.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a proposal or intention for what to do, the same as a scheme or design.

clue.text: This woman comes to order lemon cheese

indicators.note: putting things to order means arranging them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the letters that join the name; taking them away leaves the name's letters

explanation.surface: A woman arrives to order some lemon-flavoured cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: this woman plus COMES, rearranged, makes LEMON CHEESE. So strike C, O, M, E, S from LEMON CHEESE and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Hélène is a French female given name, so 'this woman' points to a particular lady by name.

clue.text: Cologne No.22: are you picking up brandy?

indicators.note: picking up means catching what is heard, so the words are judged by ear

parts.note: cologne gives an odour, and V is the twenty-second letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A shopper at the perfume counter, holding a Cologne numbered 22, is asked if they are also buying spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cologne No.22' looks like a perfume's name; it is a scent (odour) plus the 22nd letter, V, said together.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie, French for water of life, is a clear fruit brandy, a distilled spirit.
